title: Fit empirical coefficients z₁–z₄
action: Fit the coefficients z₁, z₂, z₃, z₄ of the empirical relation log10 p_I₂(x,T) = z₁ + z₂·x + z₃/T + z₄·x/T using the provided phase-boundary (x,T) data. Apply the local fitting procedure: for each temperature of interest, solve the linear system formed by two nearby temperatures (|ΔT| ≤ 5 K) and their phase-boundary compositions. Store the resulting numerical relationship for use in Step 2.
description: This process step must be executed to derive the empirical p_I₂ relation. Without it the downstream scored step cannot be completed correctly. The agent may save the fitted coefficients or callable function as evidence.

title: Compute equilibrium p_I₂ for Hg-rich composition
action: For the mercury-rich composition x = 1.99, evaluate the equilibrium partial pressure of I₂(g) at each temperature T in the range 100–150 °C (step 5 °C). Use the empirical relation from Step 1 for p_I₂(x,T) together with the provided equilibrium constants Kp₁–Kp₄ to solve the coupled reaction equilibria. Write the results to the output CSV file.
description: The computed p_I₂ values for x=1.99 are the primary reproduction target. The checker will compare them pointwise against a hidden recomputed reference, verify that p_I₂ exceeds the 0.04 mbar visibility threshold only in the interval 110–130 °C, and check the maximum p_I₂ value in that range.
output_schema: CSV with columns: temperature_C (float, °C, covering 100–150 °C with step ≤ 5 K), p_I2_mbar (float, computed equilibrium partial pressure of I₂(g) in mbar).
